**Round 38: clicking a fader no longer jumps, dragging is relative, double-click resets**
- **Faders covered:** track Volume (audio tracks and the video track), Pan and Master. The Zoom slider is navigation, not a fader, and stays as it is.
- **Behaviour:**
  - Today a click jumps the value to the click point (Master to ΓêÆ27 dB, Volume to 50%) and writes an undo entry. After this round a click without movement changes nothing, writes nothing, and focuses the fader.
  - A drag moves the value relative to where it started; release writes one undo entry.
  - Double-click resets to 100% / 0.0 dB / centre.
  - Keyboard behaviour and the Pan reset button are unchanged.
- **Mechanism:** A blocks the browser's default press handling on the fader. I tested this on the live `/studio-lab`: the value stayed at 0, the browser no longer gave the fader focus, and click events still fired. Without it the value jumped to ΓêÆ27.
  - The drag reuses the existing preview/commit functions, so `ArrangementContext.tsx` and `StudioWorkspace.tsx` stay frozen.
- **Test change I authorised:** exactly 3 lines in the frozen `fader-guards.test.tsx` (l.840, the l.1597 title, l.1602). They assumed focus never moves on a press, which was never true in Chrome. Any other frozen-test failure means A stops and reports.
- **What C can and cannot prove:** C checks the no-jump click with real clicks. Drag and double-click can only be simulated in the headless browser, so a real-mouse double-click and drag is a new manual check for the Tech Lead (R38-T).
- **Ableton:** Live 12 ┬º18.1 confirms the Pan double-click reset. For Volume and Master the reset is unconfirmed. "No jump on click" has no source text, so it is a CZABA requirement, not an Ableton claim. Live's "Delete returns a control to default" (┬º42.6) is a deliberate difference: Delete on a focused fader stays a no-op, as agreed in rounds 32ΓÇô33.
